rounds.text: J.G. Chemicals is demonstrating exceptional operational momentum, evidenced by a 39% compounded sales growth and 40% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E16, E19]. The company is aggressively expanding its footprint, with new capacities at Dahej and Naidupeta set to increase total zinc oxide capacity to approximately 79,900 tons per annum [E76, E89]. This growth is supported by a robust financial foundation, as the company maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02x and a net cash surplus of INR 63.3 crores [E31, E83]. Management has clearly articulated a path to margin expansion, targeting 14% to 15% EBITDA margins through a shift toward higher-value products and an increase in non-rubber application revenues to 30% [E68, E88]. Conceded: the stock trades at a premium P/E of 25.62x and P/B of 4.01x compared to sector benchmarks [E6, E7], and institutional money flow is currently negative [E38]. Despite these valuation concerns, the company’s ability to maintain high capacity utilization exceeding 80% suggests that the market may be underestimating the earnings power of its upcoming capacity additions [E81].

J.G.Chemicals Ltd carries valuation and operational risks that are not fully supported by its underlying financial consistency, beginning with a premium pricing multiple where the P/E of 25.62x and EV/EBITDA of 18.41x sit significantly higher than sector benchmarks of 19.76x and 10.57x respectively [E6, E11]. This expensive valuation is compounded by an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend over recent periods [E26, E27], while historical returns remain modest with a 3-year low return on equity of 13.2% [E55]. Furthermore, institutional investors are scaling back their exposure, evidenced by foreign and domestic institutional holdings dropping from 6.22% to 3.77% and 3.17% to 2.12% respectively [E36, E37], alongside a negative money flow signal [E38]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02x and exhibits strong recent sales growth [E31, E58]. However, shareholder returns are negligible as the dividend yield sits at a meager 0.19% [E4], and dividend payouts have historically accounted for just 1.96% of profits over the last three years [E56].

The bear asserts that valuation multiples are unjustifiably high relative to sector benchmarks, but ignores that J.G. Chemicals backs this premium with superior profitability metrics such as a 14.1% ROA and 20.55% ROCE, which easily outshine the respective sector benchmarks of 5.67% and 11.09% [E6, E8, E10, E11]. Conceded: the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends read inconsistent over the short term [E26, E27], yet operating margins have actually expanded by 3 percentage points to 10% in the TTM period and 11% in the September 2026 quarter compared to earlier periods [E24, E25]. While institutional holdings have decreased and the dividend yield is low, the business is aggressively scaling through greenfield and brownfield expansions that take capacity to nearly 79,900 tons per annum, supported by a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02x and a comfortable current ratio of 18.64x [E4, E31, E32, E36, E37, E76]. Conceded: dividend payouts have historically been minimal at 1.96% of profits over the last three years [E56], but this reflects management reinvesting capital into high-return projects rather than returning funds to shareholders prematurely. Finally, the negative money flow and lower institutional participation overlook the fundamental business momentum, which includes a 40% TTM profit growth, a rules-based screen score of 94 out of 100, and a DCF intrinsic value suggesting a margin of safety of 37.2% [E19, E38, E40, E57].

The bull highlights superior profitability metrics, but these must be weighed against the fact that the company’s valuation is significantly stretched compared to its peers, with a P/E of 25.62x versus a sector benchmark of 19.76x and a P/B of 4.01x against 1.7x [E6, E7]. While the bull points to capacity expansion, it ignores that institutional investors are actively reducing their exposure, with foreign and domestic holdings dropping by 2.45 and 1.05 percentage points respectively, resulting in a negative money flow signal [E36, E37, E38]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong balance sheet with a 0.02x debt-to-equity ratio and 18.64x current ratio [E31, E32]. However, the bull’s reliance on TTM growth figures masks the reality that the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends remain inconsistent [E26, E27]. Furthermore, the bull justifies the low 0.19% dividend yield as reinvestment, yet this ignores the reality that the company’s cash conversion is only moderate at 0.64x, and borrowings have more than doubled from Rs 6 Cr to Rs 14 Cr in just one year [E4, E28, E33]. Finally, the bull cites a high screen score, but this fails to account for the 50.8% annualised volatility and the historical record of a -41.7% peak-to-trough drawdown, suggesting that the current price levels carry significant risk [E47, E48, E57].

The bear’s focus on valuation multiples ignores that J.G. Chemicals is fundamentally outperforming its sector, with an ROE of 15.01% versus the 9.33% benchmark and an ROCE of 20.55% against 11.09% [E9, E10]. While the bear cites institutional outflows, this ignores the company’s massive growth trajectory, including 39% sales growth and 40% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E16, E19]. Conceded: institutional holdings have declined [E36, E37, E38]. The bear’s claim of inconsistent margins overlooks the clear structural improvement, as operating margins have expanded by 3 percentage points over the last three years and the last year alone [E24, E25]. Regarding the balance sheet, the company remains conservatively financed with a 0.02x debt-to-equity ratio, and the increase in borrowings is negligible given the massive liquidity provided by an 18.64x current ratio [E31, E32, E33]. Conceded: the dividend yield is low at 0.19% and cash conversion is moderate at 0.64x [E4, E28]. Finally, the bear’s emphasis on volatility ignores the company’s dominant market position as India’s largest player with 77,000 metric tons of capacity and a clear, management-backed roadmap to increase EBITDA margins to 14-15% through high-value product expansion [E68, E80, E86].

The bull points to superior returns on equity and capital [E9, E10], but glosses over the company's own historical disclosures showing a lower 3-year average ROE of 13.2% [E55] and a negligible dividend payout of just 1.96% of profits [E56]. While the bull celebrates TTM sales and profit growth [E16, E19], it ignores that 3-year compounded sales growth slows down to 8% and profit growth drops to 7% [E15, E18], exposing the recent spikes as cyclical bursts rather than sustainable baselines. Conceded: operating margins have ticked up over specific periods [E24, E25], but filed statements explicitly categorize the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends as inconsistent [E26, E27]. The bull dismisses institutional selling, yet foreign and domestic institutions have cut their stakes [E36, E37] alongside negative money flow signals [E38], and borrowings have more than doubled from Rs 6 Cr to Rs 14 Cr [E33]. Finally, relying on management's future margin targets [E68] ignores external vulnerabilities like West Asia disruptions [E84] and geopolitical conflicts that directly impact the supply chains of primary raw materials like zinc dross [E85].

evidence.quote: So I think on a blended basis, we are confident that in the next 3 years or so, we should be closer to the 14% to 15% EBITDA margin with the share of value-added products increasing.

evidence.fact: The company expects EBITDA margins to reach approximately 14% with higher-value product offerings.
evidence.quote: Margins as our CFO just mentioned, it would be approximately close to 14% EBITDA because stronger products are being developed, and over the last quarter, we've also invested, as we said, and come out with one or two new products, and another product is also on the anvil in which we are expecting the patent to come very soon.

evidence.fact: Utilization at the Dahej plant is expected to be between 50% and 60% in the first full financial year of operations.
evidence.quote: So, I just mentioned in the previous question that in FY28, we expect a utilization of 50% to 60% minimum, and the following year, we expect to be in the in the 70s range, and by then we would start the expansion of Phase 2.

evidence.fact: Management noted strong demand across all customer end-user applications in Q3.
evidence.quote: Even currently in Q3, we are witnessing strong demand across all our customer end-user applications, and we are confident of surpassing the numbers achieved till now.

evidence.fact: Non-rubber applications accounted for over 18% of sales in the first half of 2027.
evidence.quote: Non-rubber applications today account for over 18% of our sales in the first half of 2027, supported by expansion across ceramic, specialty chemicals, agriculture and pharmaceutical verticals.

evidence.fact: The automotive industry maintained strong momentum in Q2 FY27 supported by festive demand and significant volume growth across vehicle categories.
evidence.quote: The automotive industry maintained strong momentum in Q2 FY27, supported by festive demand.

evidence.fact: Phase 1 of the Dahej greenfield project is nearing completion with trial runs scheduled for next month.
evidence.quote: Phase 1, comprising approximately 15,000 metric tons per annum of zinc oxide capacity within the planned 40,000-plus metric tons facility, is nearing completion now with trial runs scheduled for next month.

evidence.fact: The Naidupeta brownfield expansion is on track for commissioning in Q4 of '27 and is expected to add approximately 5,000 metric tons.
evidence.quote: At Naidupeta, our brownfield expansion remains on track for commissioning in the Q4 of '27. The project is expected to add approximately 5,000 metric tons to our existing manufacturing capacity.

evidence.fact: Together, the Dahej and Naidupeta expansions are expected to increase total zinc oxide capacity to approximately 79,900 tons per annum.
evidence.quote: Together with Dahej and Naidupeta expansions are expected to increase our total zinc oxide capacity to approximately 79,900 tons per annum, providing capacity to support anticipated demand through FY28 and '29.

evidence.fact: Consolidated EBITDA margin for Q2 FY27 stood at 10.71%.
evidence.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR38.65 crores, up 77% year-on-year and 7% sequentially with an EBITDA margin of 10.71%.

evidence.fact: For the first half of the year, EBITDA margin stood at 11.07%.
evidence.quote: EBITDA was at INR74.9 crores, up 66% year-on-year with an EBITDA margin of 11.07%.

evidence.fact: For the first half of the year, PAT margin stood at 7.99%.
evidence.quote: The PAT margin for the half year ended was 7.99%.

evidence.fact: JGC has an installed capacity of almost 77,000 metric tons per annum.
evidence.quote: As India's largest player in the industry with an installed capacity of almost 77,000 metric tons per annum, JGC is very well positioned to benefit from this consolidation trend going forward.

evidence.fact: Zinc oxide capacity utilization exceeded 80% during Q2.
evidence.quote: On the operational front, the company continued to deliver double-digit volume growth during Q2 with zinc oxide capacity utilization exceeding 80%.

evidence.fact: The company has an installed capacity of 10,000 metric tons for zinc sulphate.
evidence.quote: We have installed a capacity of 10,000 metric tons for zinc sulphate.

evidence.fact: The company had a net cash surplus of INR63.3 crores as of 30th September 2026.
evidence.quote: We have a net cash surplus of INR63.3 crores as per 30th September 2026.

evidence.fact: Management noted West Asia disruptions as part of the operating environment context for tyre exports.
evidence.quote: Despite West Asia disruptions, Indian tyre majors are progressing with approximately ₹25,000 crore of announced capex to meet growing OEM and replacement demand and expand exports, which account for around 25% of Indian tyre production.

evidence.fact: Geopolitical conflict impacted global supply chains for zinc dross, the primary raw material.
evidence.quote: As we had mentioned earlier, the ongoing geopolitical conflict had impacted global supply chains for Zinc Dross, which is our primary raw material.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 3 years): Management aims to reach an EBITDA margin closer to 14% to 15% in 3 years.
evidence.quote: So I think on a blended basis, we are confident that in the next 3 years or so, we should be closer to the 14% to 15% EBITDA margin with the share of value-added products increasing.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (2028): Phase 2 of the Dahej facility is planned to start in the 2028 calendar year.
evidence.quote: Company's commitment -- so Phase 2 of the Dahej would start sometime in 2028 calendar year.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 2 to 3 years): Management targets increasing the contribution of non-rubber revenues to close to 30% over the next 2 to 3 years.
evidence.quote: So I think in the next 2 to 3 years, we should be at a level close to 30% and on the margin front, this will definitely act as a contributor in pushing up the EBITDA margins to the 14% to 15% range that we have targeted.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): New capacities in Gujarat and Naidupeta are expected to be commissioned during FY27.
evidence.quote: New capacities in Gujarat and Naidupeta are expected to be commissioned during FY27, positioning the Company to meet anticipated demand growth from the tyre sector and other end-user industries.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (Q4 FY27): The Naidupeta brownfield expansion remains on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27.
evidence.quote: The Naidupeta brownfield expansion remains on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27.
